reason: Avalon_Delaware_Fiduciary_Memo.docx s.I, III.B and VI: the board's risk is framed as abdication, independence and duty of care ('Deferring to a valid veto is not a breach in itself'; 'Business judgment review is the likely starting point'; 'Most of the exposure sits with Marcus'); loyalty and bad faith are never applied to the board. The item is itself the legal conclusion (rule 7). Expert states it (Conclusion, first bullet: 'may have breached its fiduciary duty of loyalty ... and/or acting in bad faith').

Memo III.A.1-2 describes the Chancery Moelis ruling, then lists s.122(18) as one of 'Two later developments ... enacted by Senate Bill 313'; no sentence says it was enacted in response to Moelis (no 'response' wording anywhere in the file). Causal link is implied by sequence only. Expert para 18: 'in response to the decision in Moelis, Delaware amended the DGCL'. Web tools were on.

Memo III.A.1 says bylaws cannot depart from s.141(a) because of s.109(b); III.A.3(a) ties the s.122(18) limit to the certificate, but treats 'Avalon's language' as one and never concludes that the bylaw clause cannot disable s.122(18). Expert para 19 states it ('s.122(18) speaks only of conflict with the certificate ... by-laws are subordinate').

Memo III.C says 'a controller owes fiduciary duties when it exercises stockholder power' and VI says Marcus's exposure 'rests on his status as a controller', but no sentence states the default rule that stockholders generally owe no fiduciary duties; it is only presupposed. Expert para 24 opens with that rule.

Memo III.C.2 recites the Sears duty of care (gross negligence) in general terms and III.C.3(b) calls 'intent or indifference' the contested point, but never says that refusing to consider the merits can be grossly negligent absent intent. III.C.3(e) relies on amended s.144(d)(5) (2025, newer than the rubric), which removes money damages for a controller's care breach. Expert para 26 states the item.

NoxaPulse_Share_Subscription_Agreement.docx s.6.1 and 6.3: Top-Up Shares are bought by the Investor 'at the Top-Up Price ... equal to the Dilutive Price', paid 'in cash'; Schedule II example shows $1.00 per share. Not at no cost. Expert s.4.3(a): 'issue to the Investor, for no additional consideration'.

Model Article 3 (ss.3.1-3.22) has no solvency representation; 'insolvency' appears only in the enforceability exception (3.2, 4.1), a consent matter (8.1(b)) and a notice event (9.3(l)). Expert has 'No Default or Insolvency ... The Company is not insolvent'.

Model s.5.10: the Company reimburses the Investor's legal and tax adviser fees up to $[cap]; 'Except as set forth in this Section 5.10, each Party shall bear its own costs'. The investor's main deal cost is shifted to the Company, so the item as written is not met; a capped investor-counsel reimbursement is a customary investor-side term, the task was silent, and Note to Draft item 8 flags it. Expert s.'Expenses': each party bears its own.

Model s.6.4(a) exempts shares 'issued as a dividend or distribution on, or in a stock split, subdivision, or combination of' Common Stock made pro rata; s.6.6 covers 'recapitalization, reclassification, or similar event' leaving the ownership percentage unaffected. The word 'reclassification' is not in 6.4 itself. Expert's list ('stock splits, stock dividends and similar pro rata recapitalizations') also omits it.

No prevailing-party clause in the model (no 'prevailing' in the file; Articles 12-13 read in full). Attorneys' fees appear only inside 'Losses' for mutual breach indemnities (ss.12.2-12.3), which do not reach a successful defendant. Expert s.'Expenses': 'the prevailing Party shall be entitled to recover its reasonable attorneys' fees'.

SCRA_3937_3919_Audit_Test_Questions.xlsx E8 (SCRA-12d): 'written notice with a copy of the military orders (or other appropriate indicator of service), provided within 180 days after release' has notice, orders and 180 days, but no orders extending service anywhere in the workbook. s.3937(b)(1)(A) includes 'any orders further extending military service'. Expert leading question has 'and/or extending service' and MIR-25 has the 180 days.

Model E5/D5 (SCRA-12a): cap 'for the entire period of military service'; E6/G6 (SCRA-12b): mortgage-type obligations 'through the first anniversary of ... release', NA where 'not a mortgage-type obligation'; Instructions C22 labels 12a as the non-mortgage rule. The distinction is made across the pair, not in one sentence. Expert MIR-25 covers mortgages only.
